doc.title: Arthur Davis and Andy Mosley Interview, 1960-01-12

title: Mule songs played back: Johnny Butler and Louisiana
summary: Allen plays record tracks, including Johnny Butler and a mule song, while the inmates identify singers such as Louisiana, Pete and Thomas.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: I just cut this short a minute now. I can't. That's your mule, that's your mule. Man that mule will be run around mule and be my nune this mone.
Now which one is you? That's Louisiana. That's Louisiana. I'll tell you what, man. That's your mule. That's your mule. That's your mule.
That's your mule. That's your mule. That's your mule and you better catch it too. We're flying on Luella's bottom this mone. That's right. That's my mule.

I ain't gonna water that man. French fish, you an old fish. The scales on you done got dry man. I don't know what you talking about. You oughta take my mule baby. Mule you better catch it on. I got mine, I'm gone. What is the mule weasel? I got mine, they ain't going anywhere. That's right.
That's Pete and Thomas in the night.
I got a long way to go.
I told him about a boy. To break some hands along. The wank he gon' pour the world. He gon' put salt in the back. Will you come back again? I hope so.
